sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when another vehicle is stopped at a crosswalk?
options: Pass the vehicle carefully on the right
Honk your horn and pass on the left
Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk because a pedestrian may be crossing
Pass at no more than 10 mph if you do not see anyone
explanation: You must never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk, as there may be pedestrians crossing that you cannot see.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond when approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog at an intersection?
options: Honk briefly so the pedestrian knows where your vehicle is located
Stop in the middle of the crosswalk so they can walk behind your car
Yield the right-of-way at all times and do not honk your horn
Proceed immediately unless the pedestrian waves you to stop
explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way at all times, and you should never honk your horn at them or block the crosswalk.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles meet on a steep, narrow mountain road where neither can pass, who has the right-of-way?
options: The vehicle facing downhill
The vehicle facing uphill
The heavier vehicle
The vehicle closest to the mountain wall
explanation: The vehicle facing uphill has the right-of-way because the vehicle facing downhill has more control when backing up the hill.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: How can you tell if you are driving in a large truck's blind spot ('No Zone')?
options: You cannot see the truck's side mirrors
You are more than 400 feet behind the truck
You can clearly see the truck driver's face in the side mirror
The truck is driving in the far-right lane
explanation: If you cannot see the truck's side mirrors, the truck driver cannot see your vehicle.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed at which you may pass a bus, streetcar, or trolley stopped at a safety zone or traffic light?
options: 5 mph
10 mph
15 mph
25 mph
explanation: When a bus, streetcar, or trolley is stopped at a safety zone or traffic light, you may pass at no more than 10 mph.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is true regarding sharing the road with motorcycles in California?
options: Drivers may pass a motorcycle within the same lane if there is room
Lane splitting by motorcycles is legal, and drivers should allow at least a three-second following distance
Motorcycles need a two-second following distance because they stop slower than cars
Lane splitting is illegal on all California freeways
explanation: Lane splitting is legal in California, and drivers should maintain at least a three-second following distance and never pass a motorcycle in the same lane.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: What is the law regarding following an emergency vehicle that has its siren or flashing lights on?
options: You may follow within 100 feet to get through traffic
It is illegal to follow within 300 feet of the emergency vehicle
You must stay at least 500 feet behind it only on freeways
You may follow closely as long as you do not pass it
explanation: It is against the law to follow within 300 feet of any emergency vehicle when its siren or flashing lights are active.

sectionTitle: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
question: When passing a bicyclist traveling in the same direction, how much space must you leave between your vehicle and the bicyclist?
options: At least 2 feet
At least 3 feet
At least 5 feet
At least 10 feet
explanation: California law requires drivers to allow at least three feet of space between their vehicle and a bicyclist when passing.
